title: Product-closed triangulated classes contain first-quadrant column totals
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with its ordinary derived category and localization $Q:\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in the indexing universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume countable products exist in $\mathcal A$ and that, for every countable family of complexes, the termwise product represents their product in $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-category-product]. Let $\mathcal H$ be a full replete class in $D(\mathcal A)$ containing zero and closed under all integer shifts, distinguished-triangle extensions [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], and countable derived products. Let $D^{p,q}$ be a first-quadrant double complex, with commuting horizontal and vertical differentials, and put
$$T^r=\bigoplus_{p+q=r}D^{p,q},\qquad d_T=d_I+(-1)^p d_{II}$$
[def-sp-double-complex-total]. If $Q(D^{p,\bullet})\in\mathcal H$ for every $p\geq0$, then $QT\in\mathcal H$. Zero columns and the zero double complex are included. No closure under truncations, cohomology objects, arbitrary inverse limits or arbitrary unbounded totalizations is assumed.

source.place: Tag 012Z, definition-associated-simple-complex, for the total and column filtration; agent consequence from the finite-column quotient tower and its degreewise split Roos sequence. Also extracted from lem-sfb-supported-hull-proetale-descent proof steps 8–9, without using that proof as a cited theorem.

proof.text: Put $F^nT=\bigoplus_{p\ge n}D^{p,\bullet-p}$ for $n\ge0$ and $B_n=T/F^nT$. The filtration of [def-sp-double-complex-total] is by subcomplexes: $d_I$ raises the column index and $d_{II}$ preserves it. Thus $B_n^r=\bigoplus_{0\le p<n}D^{p,r-p}$, with the total differential followed by projection to these columns. The maps $\pi_n:T\to B_n$ and $f_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ are chain maps and $f_n\pi_{n+1}=\pi_n$. Also $B_0=0$. For $r\ge0$, $\pi_n^r$ is the canonical identity on all nonzero summands once $n\ge r+1$; for $r<0$ every term is zero.

The kernel of $f_n$ is the single surviving column $C_n^r=D^{n,r-n}$ with differential $(-1)^nd_{II}$, so $C_n=D^{n,\bullet}[-n]$ with the shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The sequence $0\to C_n\to B_{n+1}\xrightarrow{f_n}B_n\to0$ is split in each degree by the inclusion of the first $n$ summands (these sections need not be chain maps). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Induct on $n$: $QB_0=0\in\mathcal H$; if $QB_n\in\mathcal H$, then $QC_n\in\mathcal H$ by the column hypothesis and shift closure, and the distinguished triangle $QC_n\to QB_{n+1}\to QB_n\to QC_n[1]$ gives $QB_{n+1}\in\mathcal H$ by extension closure. This proves the assertion for every finite column quotient.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, applied to finite-column quotient sequences

proof.text: Form the termwise product complex $P=\prod_{n\ge0}B_n$, with componentwise differential; its square is zero after every product projection. Define $s:P\to P$ by $\operatorname{pr}_ns=f_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$ and $u=1-s$. The chain equations for the $f_n$ imply that $s$ and $u$ are chain maps. Compatibility of the $\pi_n$ defines a chain map $i:T\to P$ with $\operatorname{pr}_ni=\pi_n$ and $ui=0$. These constructions use only the product universal property. By the assumed representation of countable derived products by termwise products, $QP$ with these localized projections is the countable derived product of the $QB_n$. Hence $QP\in\mathcal H$.

source.place: Tag 070M, lemma-difficulty-K-injectives, product and transition-shift construction; agent specialization to the finite-column tower

proof.text: Fix a degree $r$. Let $\sigma_n^r:B_n^r\to B_{n+1}^r$ be the graded inclusion from step 2, so $f_n^r\sigma_n^r=1$. Define maps $a_n:P^r\to B_n^r$ recursively by $a_0=0$ and $a_{n+1}=\sigma_n^r(a_n-\operatorname{pr}_n)$. Then $a_n-f_n^ra_{n+1}=\operatorname{pr}_n$. The product lift $a:P^r\to P^r$ of the $a_n$ therefore satisfies $u^ra=1$, checked after every projection. Thus $u$ is split epi in every degree; no exactness of arbitrary products and no chain-level section is used.

source.place: Tag 070M, lemma-difficulty-K-injectives, split Roos sequence; explicit recursive splitting

proof.text: The map $i^r:T^r\to P^r$ is a kernel of $u^r$. For $r<0$ all objects are zero. For $r\ge0$, let $Z$ be any object and $b:Z\to P^r$ satisfy $u^rb=0$, and write $b_n=\operatorname{pr}_nb$. Then $b_n=f_n^rb_{n+1}$. Set $N=r+1$ and $c=(\pi_N^r)^{-1}b_N:Z\to T^r$. For $n<N$, repeated compatibility gives $b_n=\pi_n^rc$. For $n\ge N$ the transitions are identities under the canonical identifications $B_n^r=T^r$, so the same equality holds. Product uniqueness gives $b=i^rc$; uniqueness of $c$ follows from projection $N$. Together with step 4 this proves that $0\to T\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{u}P\to0$ is degreewise short exact in the abelian category.

source.place: Tag 070M, lemma-difficulty-K-injectives, split Roos sequence; agent kernel identification using degreewise stabilization

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to step 5 to get the distinguished triangle $QT\to QP\to QP\to QT[1]$. Inverse rotation, which is (TR2) of [def-weil-triangulated-category], gives a distinguished triangle $QP[-1]\to QT\to QP\to QP$. Both outside terms lie in $\mathcal H$ by step 3 and shift closure; extension closure therefore gives $QT\in\mathcal H$. The same induction and product maps apply when any columns vanish, and when $D=0$ all complexes constructed above are zero.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NI-dfe2f75b7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all six steps in full. There are no new nodes, and the item is not a 2026-10-21 re-split, since it had no proof on the base. The statement is unchanged and true; I tested D=0, a single column (T = D^{p,•}[-p]) and finitely many columns. Cited statements read: def-sp-double-complex-total (sign d_I+(-1)^p d_II, filtration by subcomplexes, graded piece D^{p,•-p} with differential (-1)^p d_II); def-weil-abstract-derived-category (K[1]^r = K^{r+1} with differential -d, so K[-n] has differential (-1)^n d, which matches C_n in step 2); lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle (status mathlib, Stacks 0152, any degreewise short exact sequence of complexes); def-weil-triangulated-subcategory (0, shifts, 2-out-of-3, and H is replete); def-weil-triangulated-category (TR2 is an iff, so the inverse rotation in step 6 holds); def-weil-category-product; def-sp-abelian. Steps checked: step 2's induction starts at B_0 = 0 and the kernel of f_n is column n. Step 3 gives pr_n(ui) = π_n - f_nπ_{n+1} = 0. Step 4's recursion a_{n+1} = σ_n(a_n - pr_n) gives ua = 1, and the sign matches Stacks 070M. Step 5's kernel argument uses N = r+1 and the identity transitions beyond N. Step 6 uses the triangle QP[-1] → QT → QP → QP. Sources checked: Stacks tags 012Z/0152/070M in tags/tags, and derived.tex lines 10589-10629 for the split product sequence; only its elementary part is used, with no K-injectivity. No SGA source. Duplicate search (rg -L for first-quadrant with product/closure) found no duplicate; lem-sp-first-quadrant-total-extend-short-exact and lem-weil-roos-split-comparison are different statements. I accept the tool use lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle (a general Mathlib-status lemma). No changes.
